modules.name: Layer 0 data model and open-schema mapping
modules.design_question: What minimum geometry-plus-program record lets every evaluation module read one building consistently and export it losslessly to IFC 4.3, Speckle, glTF+JSON and BOT?
modules.effort: M: schema v0 plus IFC and glTF exporters about 4 person-days; Speckle and BOT mappers about 3 more (team estimate)
inputs: Imported or modelled geometry (meshes, B-reps, extrusions)
User program tags (office, residential, hotel, retail, cultural/civic, public, amenity, mechanical, core)
CRS and true-north record written by P14-M03
outputs: Layer0 JSON document with typed ports: Site, Tower, Level, ProgramVolume, ContextBuilding, Assumption
Per-level, per-tag floor-area table
IFC 4.3 export (IfcSite > IfcBuilding > IfcBuildingStorey > IfcSpace)
Speckle version, GLB with metadata, BOT Turtle graph
Result-card provenance fields (source_id, snapshot hash)

parameters.name: Spatial hierarchy depth
parameters.relationship: Finer Site > Building > Storey > Space records make per-floor metrics (area by use, core ratio, daylight) computable but raise tagging effort. BOT and IFC both model Site, Building, Storey and Space, so the hierarchy maps one-to-one.

parameters.name: Program vocabulary (9 tags)
parameters.relationship: More tags give a finer use split of floor area but each needs an IFC mapping; fewer tags reduce disagreement between users. Tags must roll up to the brief's use groups.

parameters.name: Employment-area flag per tag
parameters.relationship: The brief requires at least 9.0 FSR of non-residential, high-employment area (about 103,200 m2 on the 11,468 m2 site, derived). Which tags count changes the shortfall; the brief names office and commercial, so hotel and civic are open.

parameters.name: Geometry carrier (display mesh vs exact B-rep)
parameters.relationship: Triangle meshes approximate curved faces, so area and volume error grows with tessellation tolerance; exact B-rep keeps volume but is heavy in a browser. Speckle likewise separates display meshes from source objects.

parameters.name: Z origin and height definition
parameters.relationship: Tower height and storey count both depend on where Z = 0 sits. CTBUH measures from the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance, so a different zero changes height against the 244-305 m range.

parameters.name: Identity scheme (GlobalId plus applicationId)
parameters.relationship: Stable ids let tags, versions and diffs survive re-import. IFC rooted entities carry a GUID and Speckle keys objects by applicationId, so storing both keeps tags attached after the source model is edited.

parameters.name: Internal length unit (metres)
parameters.relationship: glTF fixes linear units to metres and Speckle 2026.9 keeps units per object. Storing metres removes a conversion for web viewers; each import converts once and records the source unit.

metrics.name: Mandatory-field completeness
metrics.good: 100% of required fields present (site polygon, Z origin, at least one tower, storeys with elevation, every volume with one tag)
metrics.bad: Any gap: dependent modules show a provisional label
metrics.method: JSON Schema validation on every write
metrics.basis: Required fields are our own schema v0 definition

metrics.name: IFC round-trip fidelity
metrics.good: 100% of ids, tags, units and storey links survive export then re-import with IfcOpenShell and web-ifc
metrics.bad: Any tag, id or unit lost
metrics.method: Automated test on each test model, diffing before and after
metrics.basis: Team test criterion

metrics.name: Mapping coverage
metrics.good: Every Layer 0 class has an IFC, Speckle, glTF and BOT target documented
metrics.bad: Any class without a documented target
metrics.method: Coverage matrix generated from the mapping table
metrics.basis: Own mapping table; target schemas from the cited sources

visualization: Schema browser: tree Site > Tower > Level > Volume with object counts
Coverage matrix: rows are Layer 0 classes, columns IFC / Speckle / glTF / BOT; green mapped, amber custom property set, red missing
Type badges on canvas node ports; clicking a badge opens the schema clause and its source
modules.method: Define Layer 0 as a JSON Schema with classes Site, Tower, Level, ProgramVolume, ContextBuilding and Assumption. Geometry is metre-unit triangle meshes plus an optional reference to exact source geometry. Each object stores id, source_file, source_id, tag, tag_origin (human/rule/AI), confidence, units, and level membership as a relation (as in Speckle 2026.9). Mapping: Site to IfcSite and bot:Site; Tower to IfcBuilding and bot:Building; Level to IfcBuildingStorey and bot:Storey; ProgramVolume to IfcSpace (IfcSpatialZone for overlapping zones) and bot:Space or bot:Zone. Metadata travels in a custom IFC property set, glTF extras (EXT_structural_metadata once stable), Speckle properties and BOT triples. Exporters are pure functions; CI re-imports every export with IfcOpenShell and web-ifc and diffs the result. Result cards carry source ids so any number traces to a source or a labelled team assumption.
modules.human_judgment: Which tag a volume gets, which tags count as non-residential employment area, and how storeys are defined stay with the designer; the schema only records the decision and its origin.
modules.limits: Mapping massing volumes to IfcSpace rather than IfcBuildingElementProxy is a convention I could not check against buildingSMART pages (HTTP 403). EXT_structural_metadata is a draft and BOT a W3C community draft. Speckle's 2026.9 bundle format replaced the old object graph (compatibility window ends 1 Nov 2026). Schema v0 will change after first VTC test models.

libraries.name: web-ifc
libraries.role: IFC parse and export in browser

modules.name: Multi-format import pipeline
modules.design_question: Which route gets each file type (.3dm, OBJ, IFC, glTF/FBX, SketchUp, Revit) into Layer 0 with units, hierarchy and metadata preserved, and what is lost on each?
modules.effort: L: core adapters (3dm, OBJ, IFC, glb) about 7 person-days; SketchUp/Revit export guidance cards 1 day; Speckle and APS routes about 4 more in v1 (team estimate)
outputs: Layer 0 draft: meshes, raw property bag per object, source provenance
Import report: objects read, skipped and why, units, warnings
Source-file hash for P14-M06
Raw layer paths, names and IFC classes for P14-M04

parameters.name: Source unit
parameters.relationship: OBJ stores no unit, so a wrong guess scales the model by 1,000 (mm) or 3.28 (ft) and breaks the 244-305 m range. rhino3dm exposes ModelUnitSystem, glTF is metres, and SketchUp's OBJ export has a unit drop-down.

parameters.name: Tessellation tolerance
parameters.relationship: Coarser tolerance gives fewer triangles and faster loads but larger area and volume error on curved facades. .3dm B-reps need meshes saved in the file because rhino3dm bindings show only per-face GetMesh, no Brep-to-mesh call.

parameters.name: Import route per format
parameters.relationship: Native readers keep file fidelity but exist only for 3dm, OBJ, IFC and glTF. SketchUp and Revit need a vendor export or connector, which adds a user step but preserves names, layers and properties.

parameters.name: IFC schema of the exporter (2x3 / 4 / 4x3)
parameters.relationship: web-ifc enumerates IFC2X3, IFC4 and IFC4X3, but the IfcOpenShell README claims extensive geometry support only for IFC2x3 and IFC4 Add2, so exporting IFC4 from authoring tools is the lower-risk path for towers.

parameters.name: Layer and name filter
parameters.relationship: Dropping furniture, annotation and context layers cuts triangles and mis-tagging; keeping everything preserves provenance but slows load and pollutes floor-area sums.

parameters.name: Metadata retention
parameters.relationship: Retained properties feed P14-M04 labelling. Connectors differ: Rhino sends name, colour, user strings; SketchUp custom attributes; Revit category, family, type, level and parameters.

metrics.name: Object accounting
metrics.good: 100% of source objects imported or listed as skipped with a reason
metrics.method: Count source objects against imported plus skipped
metrics.basis: Team rule: nothing disappears without a record

metrics.name: Volume parity with source application
metrics.good: <= 1% difference between imported mesh volume and source-reported volume
metrics.method: Compare signed mesh volume with the volume the user reads from Rhino, SketchUp or IFC quantities
metrics.basis: Team assumption; no source threshold found

metrics.name: IFC import time (<= 50 MB, mid-range laptop)
metrics.good: <= 10 s to meshes, in a worker
metrics.method: Time web-ifc open plus mesh extraction
metrics.basis: web-ifc benchmark on an Apple M1: 29-70 MB files opened in 0.45-1.2 s and meshed in 4.6-7.6 s; student laptops will be slower, so thresholds are padded

metrics.name: UI responsiveness during import (INP p75)
metrics.method: Event timing while a worker imports
metrics.basis: web.dev INP thresholds

metrics.name: Peak memory of an import
metrics.bad: >= 4 GiB (wasm32 ceiling, from general knowledge, not from an opened page)
metrics.method: performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory or WASM heap size
metrics.basis: Team assumption; 4 GiB limit unverified

visualization: Import report panel: one row per source object with status chips (imported, merged, skipped) and reason
Unit-detection banner showing candidate scales and the resulting site bounding box against 79.2 x 144.8 m
3D preview coloured by import status (green ok, amber heuristic, red skipped) plus triangle count per layer bar chart
modules.method: Sniff format, then run an adapter in a Web Worker that emits one intermediate ImportedObject list. .3dm: rhino3dm File3dm read, layers with paths, object names and attributes, instance definitions, ModelUnitSystem, EarthAnchorPoint; use saved render meshes through BrepFace.GetMesh and report B-reps lacking them. IFC: web-ifc mesh streaming plus property sets; IfcOpenShell server fallback for IFC4X3 or oversized files. OBJ: parse groups and usemtl, require a unit. glTF/GLB: three.js GLTFLoader, read extras. FBX: loader or assimp, unit prompt. SKP and RVT: accept only exported OBJ/GLB/IFC or Speckle versions and show an export how-to card. The list then passes through P14-M03 (units, georeference) and P14-M05 (health) before it is written to Layer 0.
modules.human_judgment: Choosing the source unit when detection is ambiguous, deciding which layers are building versus context or clutter, and accepting skipped objects.
modules.limits: Browsers cannot read .skp or .rvt natively: the SketchUp C SDK needs developer registration and Trimble terms; Revit is proprietary. Rhino.Compute code is MIT but needs Rhino 8 for Windows and core-hour billing (USD 0.10 per core-hour), not available to Educational licences. OBJ loses hierarchy and metadata. Speckle connectors do not transfer image textures.

libraries.role: GLTF, OBJ, FBX parsing (loader list not confirmed on repo page)

libraries.name: Online 3D Viewer
libraries.role: Reference importer: 3dm, obj, ifc, fbx, gltf, step (no skp)

libraries.name: Speckle connectors and file importers
libraries.role: Rhino 7-8 (Windows), SketchUp 2021-2026, Revit 2023-2027 (Windows) to Speckle versions

libraries.name: rhinomcp (MCP server)
libraries.role: Lets Claude Code inspect and clean a Rhino model before export

libraries.name: APS Model Derivative

modules.name: Units, true north and georeferencing
modules.design_question: Where is the model on Earth, and which way is north? Fix units, anchor the site in EPSG:26910, reconcile the plan's rotated north arrow with true north.
modules.effort: S-M: about 3 person-days for unit detection, north picker and IfcMapConversion export (team estimate)
inputs: Layer 0 draft and import report (declared units)
Site boundary polygon; optional City parcel polygons from P14-M08 for snapping
North-arrow bearing: two points clicked on the plan, or IFC TrueNorth, or Rhino ModelNorth
Any IfcMapConversion / IfcProjectedCRS or Rhino EarthAnchorPoint in the file
outputs: Georeference record: crs EPSG:26910, origin easting/northing/height, true_north_deg, grid_convergence_deg, ground_to_grid_scale, LoGeoRef level
Unit scale factor applied
Street-grid bearing estimate (deg from true north)
IfcMapConversion + IfcProjectedCRS for export; local-to-map 4x4 matrix
True-north vector for sun and wind modules

parameters.name: Declared source unit
parameters.relationship: Scales every coordinate: a mm/m slip changes tower height 1,000-fold, ft/m 3.28-fold. Detection tests candidate scales against the brief's 79.2 x 144.8 m site (260 x 475 ft). rhino3dm exposes ModelUnitSystem; glTF is always metres.

parameters.name: True-north angle (model north vs +Y)
parameters.relationship: Rotates every sun-path, shadow and wind-direction result by the same angle. A 1 degree error moves the tip of a 100 m shadow by about 1.7 m (100 x tan 1 degree, derived).

parameters.name: Street-grid skew (grid bearing vs true north)
parameters.relationship: The brief's north arrow is rotated relative to the street grid, so a model aligned to the grid must still carry true north separately, or all solar results rotate by the skew. The skew value is unresolved.

parameters.name: CRS and datums
parameters.relationship: Horizontal EPSG:26910 (NAD83 / UTM 10N, metres). Mixing WGS84 basemaps with NAD83 City data can shift positions 2-4 m (EPSG transformation accuracy). City LiDAR heights use CGVD28GVRD; a local Z = 0 at the entrance floor sidesteps vertical datum mixing.

parameters.name: Ground-to-grid scale
parameters.relationship: UTM scales distances by about 0.9996 near the zone centre, so areas shrink about 0.08%: roughly 83 m2 on the brief's 103,200 m2 minimum (derived). Compute areas in local ground units and store the scale for IfcMapConversion.

parameters.name: Model origin
parameters.relationship: UTM northings near 5.46 million m exceed float32 resolution (about 0.5 m steps, derived), so raw coordinates jitter in WebGL. A site-local origin keeps precision; three-mesh-bvh documents errors for large off-centre geometry.

metrics.name: Unit plausibility
metrics.good: Site bounding box within +/-2% of 79.2 x 144.8 m after scaling
metrics.bad: Off by 3x or more, or tower height outside 244-305 m, signalling a unit error
metrics.method: Compare bounding box with the brief site after each candidate scale
metrics.basis: Brief gives approximate size; the 2% tolerance is a team assumption

metrics.name: True-north error
metrics.method: Difference between the plan's north-arrow bearing and the confirmed true north (IFC TrueNorth, Rhino ModelNorth or user)
metrics.basis: Team assumption; 1 degree moves a 100 m shadow tip about 1.7 m (derived geometry)

metrics.name: Georeference level (LoGeoRef)
metrics.bad: 20 or lower: single latitude/longitude, no rotation
metrics.method: Inspect the IFC attributes present; emit IfcMapConversion on export
metrics.basis: Level definitions from the City2BIM wiki; the target level is a team choice

metrics.name: Site position agreement with City parcels
metrics.bad: > 2 m, which suggests a datum mix-up
metrics.method: Distance between placed site corners and the nearest City parcel vertices
metrics.basis: EPSG lists NAD83-to-WGS84 transformation accuracy of 2-4 m; 0.5 m is a team assumption

visualization: Plan view with three labelled arrows (true north, grid north, plan north) and their angles
Site outline over City parcel polygons with a distance heat-line
Unit-detection card listing candidate scales, and a LoGeoRef 10-50 badge with a checklist of IFC attributes present
modules.method: 1) Read units: rhino3dm ModelUnitSystem, IFC IfcUnitAssignment, glTF = metres, OBJ = ask. 2) Auto-check scale: pick the candidate (1, 0.001, 0.01, 0.3048, 0.0254) that makes the site bounding box match 79.2 x 144.8 m within 2%, else ask. 3) Georeference: use Rhino EarthAnchorPoint or IFC IfcMapConversion/TrueNorth (IfcOpenShell geolocation helpers); otherwise the user picks the site corner, optionally snapped to City parcels. Transform with proj4js after registering EPSG:26910 (+proj=utm +zone=10 +datum=NAD83). 4) True north: take the arrow bearing from two clicked points; compare with grid north (convergence about delta-longitude x sin latitude, roughly 0.1 deg here, derived) and with the street-grid bearing from the dominant parcel-edge direction. 5) Emit IfcMapConversion and the local matrix; store float64, render relative to the origin.
modules.human_judgment: Confirming which north the site plan's arrow shows (true, grid or magnetic), choosing site origin and entrance level, and deciding whether to align the model to the street grid.
modules.limits: No source I could open quantifies the downtown street-grid skew or the north arrow on the organiser's plan; it may be magnetic or grid-based and must be confirmed with the organiser. The vertical datum of the organiser's plan is unknown. Georeferencing a hypothetical block is a convention, not a survey.

libraries.name: proj4js
libraries.role: Coordinate transforms; EPSG:26910 must be added with proj4.defs

modules.name: AI-assisted semantic labelling and floor detection
modules.design_question: Can layers, names, IFC classes and geometry become proposed program tags and storeys that a designer only confirms, with visible evidence and confidence?
modules.effort: M: rules plus floor detection about 5 person-days (a manual tagging fallback must exist in core); LLM stage and review queue about 4 more (team estimate)
inputs: Property bag per object (layer path, name, user strings, IFC class and psets)
Geometry summary (bounding box, area, normals, Z extents)
Optional designer examples for few-shot prompts
outputs: ProposedTag list {object_id, tag, confidence, evidence[], origin rule|AI}
Storey table {name, elevation, floor-to-floor, count}
Review queue of unresolved objects
Accepted tags written to Layer 0 with tag_origin and confidence

parameters.name: Rule layer (IFC class and layer-name dictionary)
parameters.relationship: Deterministic rules explain themselves and cover well-labelled IFC/Revit exports; coverage falls for .3dm and OBJ with ad-hoc layer names, which is where the AI step is needed.

parameters.name: AI model and structured-output schema
parameters.relationship: A JSON-schema-constrained reply guarantees parseable tags with evidence strings, but not correct ones; numeric min/max cannot be enforced in the schema, so confidence gating and human confirmation are required.

parameters.name: Auto-accept confidence threshold
parameters.relationship: A higher threshold gives fewer wrong auto-tags but more manual confirmations; items below it go to the review queue. Values are team assumptions until calibrated on a labelled set.

parameters.name: Floor-detection Z tolerance
parameters.relationship: A wider tolerance merges mezzanines and double-height floors and under-counts storeys; a narrower one splits sloped or stepped slabs into false storeys. Counting should follow CTBUH: above-ground floors, significant mezzanines, no plant above the general roof.

parameters.name: Floor-to-floor prior by use
parameters.relationship: A prior lets the detector reject spurious levels, but a wrong prior biases storey count. Typical values belong to the structure and program packets and are not sourced here.

parameters.name: Zero-level definition (entrance floor)
parameters.relationship: Which level is ground changes storey numbering and tower height; CTBUH uses the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance.

metrics.name: Tag precision on a gold set
metrics.method: Hold-out set of team-labelled models (including VTC test massings)
metrics.basis: No literature benchmark retrieved; editable preset

metrics.name: Tag coverage after confirmation
metrics.good: 100% of enclosed floor area tagged and confirmed
metrics.method: Tagged floor area divided by total enclosed floor area
metrics.basis: Team rule

metrics.name: Storey count error vs author's count
metrics.method: Detected storeys (CTBUH counting) minus the count the author states
metrics.basis: Counting rule from CTBUH; thresholds are team assumptions (off by one shown amber)

metrics.name: Human override rate
metrics.good: <= 10% of AI tags changed by the user
metrics.method: Changed tags divided by AI-proposed tags per project
metrics.basis: Team assumption; signals prompt or dictionary quality

visualization: 3D view coloured by proposed tag with a confidence gradient (opacity or hatch)
Review table sorted by lowest confidence; click zooms to the object with an evidence popover (for example 'layer L12_OFFICE matched rule R3')
Floor slices as translucent planes with elevation ticks and storey labels
modules.method: Stage 1 rules: IFC class and predefined type, Revit category/family/type, layer-path tokens and object names through an editable dictionary. Stage 2 geometry: cluster Z levels of horizontal faces (histogram plus 1-D clustering), derive storeys, assign each volume by centroid Z, compute floor-plate areas, flag vertical stacks with near-identical footprints as candidate cores. Stage 3 LLM for unresolved items: input names, layers, user strings and a geometry summary; output JSON-schema constrained tag, confidence and evidence. Stage 4 human review queue; accepted tags are stored with origin and confidence. Labels outside the Layer 0 vocabulary go to 'unclassified'. Every AI call is logged with model id, prompt hash and output so P14-M06 can show the work.
modules.human_judgment: Every proposed tag and storey is a suggestion; the designer accepts or edits it. Ambiguous uses (hotel lobby versus public space, amenity versus residential) remain a judgement.
modules.limits: No accuracy benchmark from the literature was retrieved (web-search budget ran out), so every threshold is a team assumption until measured on a labelled VTC test set. LLM output depends on model version and is not deterministic; sending project geometry to a hosted API raises confidentiality questions for competition entries.

libraries.role: IFC class filters, classification, geometry quantities

modules.name: Geometry health and Layer 0 validation
modules.design_question: Is the imported geometry closed, correctly scaled, inside plausible brief limits and tagged completely enough for evaluation modules to trust? What exactly fails, and where?
modules.effort: M: about 4 person-days for closedness, orientation, unit and envelope checks (team estimate)
outputs: Health report: severity, location and suggested fix per rule
Trust level per downstream input (pass / warn / block)
Brief precheck table (tower height, site size, per-tag floor area)
Auto-fix actions (weld, flip normals, rescale)

parameters.name: Weld tolerance
parameters.relationship: Larger tolerance closes small gaps but collapses thin features; too small leaves open edges that make volume and floor area wrong.

parameters.name: Closed-volume requirement by class
parameters.relationship: ProgramVolumes must be closed for volume and area to be valid; context surfaces and site plates may stay open without affecting shadow or wind results.

parameters.name: Brief envelope (height 244-305 m, site 79.2 x 144.8 m)
parameters.relationship: Heights or site sizes outside the envelope usually signal unit or zero-level mistakes. The brief allows justified breaches, so flags warn rather than block.

parameters.name: Overlap and gap tolerance between program volumes
parameters.relationship: Overlaps double-count floor area and gaps hide it; the tolerance sets what is flagged and therefore how reliable per-use area and FSR inputs are.

parameters.name: Analysis triangle budget
parameters.relationship: More triangles improve accuracy but slow BVH queries; three-mesh-bvh quotes 500 rays at 60 fps on an 80,000-polygon model as a reference scale.

metrics.name: Closed-manifold share of ProgramVolumes
metrics.bad: Any open volume feeding area or volume metrics
metrics.method: Edge-use count (each edge shared by exactly two faces); Brep.IsSolid and IsManifold for .3dm
metrics.basis: Team rule; rhino3dm binds IsSolid and IsManifold

metrics.name: Tower height (CTBUH architectural top)
metrics.bad: Outside the range (warn; a justified breach may be rewarded)
metrics.method: Z of architectural top minus Z of lowest significant open-air entrance floor, excluding antennas and signage
metrics.basis: VTC brief height range (PDF not independently opened); CTBUH measurement rule

metrics.name: Site bounding-box match
metrics.method: Compare site polygon bounds with the brief
metrics.basis: Brief gives approximate size; tolerances are team assumptions

metrics.name: Program overlap volume
metrics.method: Mesh Boolean intersection of volumes within each storey
metrics.basis: Team assumption

metrics.name: Tag coverage of enclosed volume
metrics.method: Tagged enclosed volume divided by total enclosed volume
metrics.basis: Team rule

visualization: 3D overlay: open edges red lines, flipped faces magenta, overlap volumes orange, out-of-envelope parts hatched
Checklist of pass/warn/block rules, each linked to its source clause (for example 'VTC brief: 244-305 m')
Trust badge on each downstream node input
modules.method: Run in a worker: (1) edge-use histogram; every edge shared by exactly two faces means closed and manifold, and for .3dm B-reps use IsSolid/IsManifold; (2) signed volume sign to detect inverted normals; (3) degenerate and duplicate faces; (4) unit sanity and brief envelope, with height measured by the CTBUH rule from the user-confirmed entrance floor to the architectural top, excluding antennas and signage; (5) program overlap and gap per storey with manifold mesh Booleans; (6) tag coverage ratio. Each rule returns severity, location and fix. 'Block' stops dependent modules; 'warn' lets them run with a provisional label shown on every result card.
modules.human_judgment: Deciding whether an open or overlapping volume is a modelling error or design intent, and whether an out-of-envelope result is a justified breach.
modules.limits: Mesh checks cannot prove design intent; open context meshes are legitimate. The brief says its documents are academic and the jury may reward justified breaches, so envelope flags are warnings. The CTBUH height rule needs the user to identify the lowest significant entrance; an automatic guess is fallible.

libraries.role: Guaranteed-manifold mesh Booleans in WASM (serial build)

modules.name: Design-state versioning and provenance ledger
modules.design_question: How are design states, assumptions and module results stored so any result can be reproduced, compared, forked and traced to sources, including flagged false assumptions that must stay visible?
modules.effort: M: snapshots, hashing and result cards about 4 person-days (minimal provenance fields ship in P14-M01 for core); diff view about 4 more; fork and merge about 5 (team estimate)
inputs: Module graph configuration (nodes on/off, parameter values, assumption overrides)
outputs: Snapshot ids (content hash) with parent links
Diff {objects added/removed/changed, tag changes, parameter changes}
Provenance graph of Entity, Activity and Agent
Result cards: 'computed from snapshot X, module vY, parameters Z'
Append-only assumption log including FALSE ASSUMPTION flags

parameters.name: Snapshot granularity (per edit / per module run / manual commit)
parameters.relationship: Finer snapshots give exact undo and reproducibility but multiply storage and noise; manual commits are cheap but results may refer to uncommitted state, so every result card must pin a snapshot.

parameters.name: Hashing and canonical form
parameters.relationship: Content hashes deduplicate identical states and expose silent changes; Speckle uses content-based identity with immutable versions. Unsorted JSON keys or unrounded floats would break hashes unless canonicalised.

parameters.name: Storage backend (Speckle / git-in-browser / custom)
parameters.relationship: Speckle brings versions, viewer and connectors, but its data format changed at 2026.9 and the Free plan keeps 100 versions with 30-day history. Browser git is free but has CORS and filesystem-ordering caveats for large blobs.

parameters.name: Module version pinning
parameters.relationship: Forked modules may change thresholds. Without module version and threshold sources stored on each result, a diff of metrics cannot tell a design change from a rule change.

parameters.name: Assumption log retention
parameters.relationship: Entries move team assumption to verified or FALSE ASSUMPTION but are never deleted; deletion would hide why earlier results changed. This is a project requirement, not an external standard.

parameters.name: Merge model (snapshot fork vs real-time sync)
parameters.relationship: Snapshot fork and three-way merge matches GitHub-like community forking and is simpler; real-time CRDT sync merges concurrent edits automatically but needs per-object conflict rules and is deferred.

metrics.name: Reproducibility
metrics.good: 100% of deterministic results regenerate with an identical output hash from snapshot plus module version
metrics.method: Nightly replay of stored result cards
metrics.basis: Course requirement to show work; threshold is a team rule

metrics.name: Provenance completeness
metrics.good: 100% of displayed numbers link to a source id and snapshot, or carry a 'team assumption' badge
metrics.bad: Any unsourced number without a badge
metrics.method: Scan result cards for missing source_ids
metrics.basis: Course requirement (every result cites its source)

metrics.name: UI latency while snapshotting or diffing (INP p75)
metrics.method: Run hashing and diff in workers; measure event timing
metrics.basis: web.dev INP thresholds

visualization: Commit graph (git-style DAG) coloured by author and fork
Two-snapshot diff: 3D ghost overlay (added green, removed red, moved amber) with a table of parameter and metric deltas
Result card chain source > snapshot > module version > metric, drawn with PROV-style arrows; FALSE ASSUMPTION entries in the special colour on the timeline
modules.method: Canonicalise Layer 0 JSON (sorted keys, floats rounded to 1e-6 m) and hash geometry blobs separately (SHA-256). A snapshot is a Merkle-style manifest {layer0_hash, geometry_hashes, graph_config_hash, assumptions_hash, parent_ids, author, time}. Diff by object id: added and removed sets, per-object hashes, then attribute diffs (tag, storey, transform). Results are stored as PROV-O: result Entity wasGeneratedBy a module-run Activity that used the snapshot and source Entities, wasAttributedTo an Agent. Forks copy manifest pointers, not geometry. Merge is three-way on Layer 0 objects with conflicts listed for a human. Optionally push snapshots to Speckle as versions via specklepy, and use IfcOpenShell ifcdiff for IFC-level comparison.
modules.human_judgment: When to commit, how to name a design state, resolving merge conflicts, and deciding when an assumption has been disproved and must be flagged.
modules.limits: Hash reproducibility holds only for deterministic modules; WASM or browser floating-point differences and LLM steps (P14-M04) break bit-exactness, so those results store the produced output instead of recomputing. Speckle Free plan keeps 100 versions and 30 days of history. Real-time co-editing is out of scope for v1.

libraries.name: isomorphic-git
libraries.role: Git in the browser for snapshots and forks

modules.name: Browser geometry kernel and performance budget
modules.design_question: Which in-browser and optional server geometry stack handles tower-scale models fast enough for interactive evaluation, and when must work move to a worker, a server or Rhino.Compute?
modules.effort: M: shell, workers, float64 store and performance HUD about 4 person-days; OpenCascade and Compute integration roadmap (team estimate)
inputs: Compute requests from modules (ray casts, sections, Booleans, area and volume)
outputs: Render mesh with LOD and analysis mesh with BVH
Section polylines and Boolean results
Performance report (ms, MB per node)
Offload-recommended flag per task

parameters.name: Tessellation tolerance and LOD
parameters.relationship: Coarser meshes speed ray casting for sun and view modules but understate curved-facade area; three-mesh-bvh's 500 rays at 60 fps on 80,000 polygons is a reference scale for analysis meshes.

parameters.name: Compute location (main thread / worker / server / Rhino.Compute)
parameters.relationship: Main-thread work over 50 ms hurts responsiveness; workers keep the canvas interactive. Rhino.Compute adds exact Rhino geometry but needs Rhino 8 for Windows and core-hour billing (USD 0.10 per core-hour), not for Educational licences.

parameters.name: Kernel choice (mesh vs B-rep vs rhino3dm)
parameters.relationship: Mesh kernels (three.js, three-mesh-bvh, manifold) are small and fast but approximate. OCCT-based opencascade.js gives exact B-rep and STEP but its WASM is large; rhino3dm reads Rhino data but has no Brep meshing call in the bindings checked.

parameters.name: Numeric precision (float64 store, origin-relative render)
parameters.relationship: UTM northings near 5.46 million m exceed float32's 0.5 m resolution (derived); subtracting a site origin before upload keeps sub-millimetre precision at tower scale.

parameters.name: Memory ceiling and streaming
parameters.relationship: Whole-file WASM loads are bounded by browser memory, while City LiDAR 2022 tiles reach 2.74 GB zipped. COPC range requests let browsers read point-cloud subsets without downloading whole tiles.

metrics.name: Input latency (INP, p75)
metrics.method: PerformanceObserver event timing during imports and slider drags
metrics.basis: web.dev INP thresholds

metrics.name: Frame work per frame
metrics.method: Render stats and performance marks while orbiting the model
metrics.basis: RAIL: produce frames in 10 ms because the browser needs about 6 ms

metrics.name: Task chunk length
metrics.method: Long Task observer
metrics.basis: RAIL: idle work in 50 ms chunks, respond within 100 ms

metrics.name: Canvas shell interactive (no model loaded)
metrics.good: <= 5 s on mid-range mobile over slow 3G; later loads < 2 s
metrics.method: Lighthouse; lazy-load rhino3dm, web-ifc and OCCT WASM after the shell
metrics.basis: RAIL load target

metrics.name: Peak WASM heap
metrics.bad: >= 4 GiB (wasm32 ceiling from general knowledge, not an opened page)
metrics.method: Heap size sampling
metrics.basis: Team assumption; ceiling unverified

visualization: Performance HUD in the canvas corner (fps, frame ms, long-task count, heap MB) with traffic-light bands from the thresholds
Per-node timing bar on each canvas node showing parse, mesh, BVH and compute time
Offload banner naming the task and the measured cost when a threshold is crossed
modules.method: Parse in a worker (rhino3dm, web-ifc) into a Float64 geometry store, subtract the site origin, and upload Float32 buffers to three.js BufferGeometry. Build an analysis mesh with decimation and a three-mesh-bvh tree. Modules call workers by RPC for ray casts (sun, view), section planes, area and volume. Use manifold-3d for mesh Booleans and validation; lazy-load opencascade.js (custom build) only when a module needs exact B-rep or STEP. Offload rule: if a task exceeds 100 ms measured, or a file exceeds the tested size, move it to a server worker running IfcOpenShell or rhino3dm.py; use Rhino.Compute only if a licensed server exists. Record timings with PerformanceObserver (longtask, event timing).
modules.human_judgment: Choosing speed versus accuracy (tessellation, offloading) and accepting approximations on curved geometry.
modules.limits: The opencascade.js repo page shows an OCCT 7.6.2 badge and no listed releases, so maintenance is unclear, and its bundle is large unless custom-built (unverified). McNeel calls rhino3dm.wasm fairly large. Benchmarks quoted are on an Apple M1 and will not match student laptops. Rhino.Compute needs Windows and Rhino 8.

libraries.name: opencascade.js
libraries.role: Exact B-rep in WASM (optional, custom build)

libraries.name: Rhino.Compute
libraries.license: MIT code; Rhino 8 for Windows licence or core-hour billing required

modules.name: City of Vancouver context ingest
modules.design_question: What surrounding buildings, terrain and protected views can be pulled from City open data, how current and accurate are they, and what must be added by hand, such as approved but unbuilt towers?
modules.effort: S-M: footprints, parcels and view cones about 3 person-days; LiDAR to COPC pipeline about 1 week, roadmap (team estimate). Skip if the organiser's 3D model already includes context.
inputs: Site location and EPSG:26910 georeference from P14-M03
outputs: ContextBuilding list {footprint, base_elev, top_elev, parts, source dataset, year, licence}
Terrain surface
View-cone polygons (24)
Parcel polygons and rapid transit lines
Context currency report
Manual-add queue for approved towers

parameters.name: Context radius
parameters.relationship: A larger radius adds distant towers that cast long shadows or channel wind but increases triangles and download. The radius needed as a function of tower height is not sourced here and belongs to the CLIM packets.

parameters.name: Height source (footprints 2009 / LiDAR 2022 / organiser model / OSM and Overture)
parameters.relationship: Footprints derive from 2009 LiDAR and are not updated, so towers built since are missing. LiDAR 2022 (about 49 points/m2, 0.081 m vertical accuracy at 95%) catches them but needs processing; Overture and OSM add newer footprints under ODbL.

parameters.name: Part handling (one building id, several polygons)
parameters.relationship: A building appears as stacked polygons with different base and top elevations. Extruding each from baseelev_m to topelev_m reproduces podium plus tower; merging by building id would overstate volume.

parameters.name: Terrain source and datum
parameters.relationship: Terrain slope sets entrance level and context base. City LiDAR uses CGVD28GVRD, which may differ from the organiser's plan, so context heights are shifted to the local Z = 0.

parameters.name: Manual additions (approved, unbuilt towers)
parameters.relationship: The brief says context includes future approved towers; no open dataset of approved massing was found, so omitting them under-predicts shadow and wind interaction.

parameters.name: Protected view cones (24 polygons)
parameters.relationship: Building heights inside cones are limited, but the dataset gives polygons only. A policy module needs by-law height limits; a tower footprint or top inside a cone may be restricted.

parameters.name: Licence and attribution
parameters.relationship: City data is under Open Government Licence - Vancouver; OSM-derived layers are ODbL (share-alike). The tool must show attribution and keep ODbL layers separable.

metrics.name: Data age
metrics.method: 2026 minus acquisition year: footprints 2009 = 17 (bad), LiDAR 2022 = 4 (good)
metrics.basis: Team assumption; ages from dataset metadata

metrics.name: Stated vertical accuracy
metrics.bad: Not stated (footprints 2009: 'approximate, best used for comparison')
metrics.method: Read from dataset metadata
metrics.basis: Team assumption; values quoted from City metadata

metrics.name: Missed tall buildings
metrics.good: 0 buildings taller than 100 m (LiDAR building class) without a matching footprint part
metrics.method: Compare LiDAR 2022 building-class heights with footprint extrusions and list unmatched peaks
metrics.basis: Team assumption; 100 m cut-off is an editable preset

metrics.name: Attribution completeness
metrics.good: 100% of context layers carry dataset id, licence and year
metrics.method: Check metadata on each context object
metrics.basis: Licence terms of the cited datasets (full City licence text not opened)

visualization: Context massing extruded from City data, coloured by data year (cool recent, warm old), with a ring at the chosen radius
View-cone polygons as translucent ground wedges with labels; LiDAR-derived terrain as hillshade
Badge per layer showing source, licence and age; suspected missing towers as dashed outlines
modules.method: Fetch GeoJSON from the City open-data API (building-footprints-2009, property-parcel-polygons, view-cones, rapid-transit-lines) within the radius; reproject WGS84 to EPSG:26910 with proj4js; group by bldgid; extrude each part from baseelev_m to topelev_m and check that topelev_m minus baseelev_m equals hgt_agl. Render relative to the site origin. Roadmap: convert LiDAR 2022 LAS tiles (up to 2.74 GB zipped) to COPC server-side, read building-class points to update heights and detect new towers. Merge the organiser's context model with priority if supplied; users add approved towers as boxes tagged 'manual, team assumption'. Every context object keeps dataset id, year and licence.
modules.human_judgment: Which context matters, adding approved-but-unbuilt towers, and deciding whether to trust an old dataset over the organiser's model.
modules.limits: Footprints 2009 are generalised and not updated; towers completed since are absent or wrong. The view-cone dataset has polygons only; allowable height surfaces are in by-laws. The meaning of avght_m and maxht_m, and the datum of topelev_m, are not documented in what I opened. The City licence text and the Higher Buildings policy PDFs could not be opened.

libraries.name: copc.js / COPC format
libraries.license: MIT (copc.js); COPC spec licence not stated on its page

libraries.name: Overture Maps buildings / OpenStreetMap
libraries.role: Newer footprints and heights as fallback

sources.title: buildingSMART IFC4.3.x-development repository
sources.extract: ifc4.3-main branch holds IFC4.3.2.0; the approved release is ISO (iso.org/standard/84123.html); formal releases are CC BY-ND 4.0; HTML docs at standards.buildingsmart.org returned HTTP 403 to my fetcher.

sources.title: Industry Foundation Classes (Wikipedia)
sources.extract: IFC registered as ISO 16739-1:2024; latest listed IFC4.3 Add2 (2024); rooted entities carry a GUID; formats IFC-SPF, ifcXML, ifcZIP, ifcJSON, IFC-Turtle (ifcOWL).

sources.title: IfcSpatialZone (IFC 4.3 documentation)
sources.extract: Not opened (redirect then HTTP 403). Known only from a search summary: non-hierarchical, possibly overlapping functional grouping such as thermal, lighting or usable-area zones.

sources.title: City2BIM IFCGeoRefChecker wiki (LoGeoRef levels)
sources.extract: LoGeoRef 10 postal address; 20 IfcSite RefLatitude/RefLongitude; 30 placement of a spatial element; 40 IfcGeometricRepresentationContext WorldCoordinateSystem plus TrueNorth; 50 IfcMapConversion plus IfcProjectedCRS (EPSG).

sources.title: IfcOpenShell repository
sources.extract: Core LGPL-3.0-or-later; parses IFC2x3, IFC4 Add2, IFC4x1, IFC4x2, IFC4x3 Add2 but README says extensive geometry support only for IFC2x3 TC1 and IFC4 Add2 TC1; includes IfcConvert, IfcClash, ifcpatch, ifcdiff.

sources.title: IfcOpenShell util/geolocation.py (v0.8.0)
sources.extract: Functions get_true_north, get_grid_north, auto_xyz2enh, auto_enh2xyz, get_helmert_transformation_parameters (IfcMapConversion, IfcRigidOperation); IFC2X3 reads ePSet_MapConversion; the util folder also has unit, classification, placement, shape and selector modules.

sources.title: web-ifc (That Open Company)
sources.extract: MPL-2.0; reads and writes IFC via WebAssembly in browser or Node; ifc-schema.ts defines Schemas IFC2X3, IFC4, IFC4X3 and entity ids including IFCBUILDINGSTOREY, IFCSPACE, IFCMAPCONVERSION, IFCPROJECTEDCRS.

sources.title: web-ifc benchmark results
sources.extract: Apple M1, 8 GB: 70 MB IFC opened in 448 ms and fully executed in 5.5 s; 29-34 MB files opened in about 1.1 s and executed in 4.6-7.6 s; 31 files, 0 errors.

sources.title: Speckle data schema overview (pre-2026.9 object graph)
sources.extract: Content-based object identity with deduplication; applicationId stable across versions; Collections hold hierarchy; DataObject displayValue holds visual meshes; a version is an immutable snapshot with message, author, source application and timestamp.

sources.title: Speckle object model overview (2026.9 bundles)
sources.extract: Bundles replace the nested object tree; units are per object; no Level object (ON_LEVEL relation); no Proxy types; compatibility mode for ACC sync and file uploads lasts until 1 November 2026; 2026.9 SDK needed to read bundles.

sources.title: Speckle Revit connector
sources.extract: Revit 2023-2027, Windows only; exports model categories with family, type, level, parameters and meshes; image textures not transferred; objects load as Direct Shapes; licence and cost not covered.

sources.title: Speckle SketchUp connector
sources.extract: SketchUp 2021-2026 on Windows and macOS; publishes components, groups, faces, lines, custom attributes and render materials; image textures not supported.

sources.title: Speckle Rhino connector
sources.extract: Rhino 7 and 8, Windows only; sends geometry with name, colour, material and user strings, blocks, layer structure; image textures not transferred; brep conversion not documented on the page.

sources.title: Speckle pricing
sources.extract: Free Explore plan: 1 project, 3 users, 100 versions, 30-day history, all file importers and connectors; free for students and educators; custom plans not priced on the page.

sources.title: speckle-server repository
sources.extract: Apache-2.0 unless stated; monorepo with server, frontend, three.js viewer, objectloader and file-import service; Docker Compose files for self-hosting.

sources.title: glTF overview
sources.extract: Royalty-free; ISO/IEC 12113:2022; JSON scene description with optional binary GLB; extensions mechanism.

sources.title: glTF 2.0 specification
sources.extract: Units for all linear distances are metres; right-handed coordinate system with +Y up and +Z forward (first 200,000 characters read; extras text not seen).

sources.title: EXT_structural_metadata (glTF extension)
sources.extract: Draft extension implementing the 3D Metadata Specification: schemas with classes and enums, property tables, property attributes and textures.

sources.title: Building Topology Ontology (BOT)
sources.publisher: W3C Linked Building Data Community Group
sources.extract: Classes Site, Building, Storey, Space, Zone, Element, Interface; properties hasStorey, hasSpace, containsElement, adjacentElement; alignment to ifcOWL provided; no licence stated for the ontology itself.

sources.title: rhino3dm repository
sources.extract: MIT; .NET, Python (CPython 3.8-3.14) and JavaScript/WASM; reads and writes .3dm, layers and attributes; client for Rhino Compute; .wasm is fairly large per the JS README.

sources.title: rhino3dm bindings (settings, brep, mesh, layer)
sources.extract: bnd_3dm_settings binds ModelUnitSystem and EarthAnchorPoint (lat, lon, elevation, model north/east); bnd_brep binds BrepFace.GetMesh, IsSolid, IsManifold but no Mesh.CreateFromBrep; bnd_layer binds name, full path, colour, visibility; no layer user strings seen. Only these files were read.

sources.title: Rhino.Compute repository and LICENSE.md
sources.extract: MIT licence (rhino.compute, Hops); built on Rhino 8 for Windows; REST API for RhinoCommon and Grasshopper.

sources.title: Rhino.Compute licensing and core-hour billing
sources.extract: USD 0.10 per core per hour while Rhino runs, pro-rated per minute; needs a dedicated licence team with no licences; not compatible with Educational or Commercial licences; token stored in RHINO_TOKEN.

sources.title: Rhino 8 index of import/export file types
sources.extract: Import and export both list skp, glb/gltf, obj, fbx, dwg, step; IFC and rvt not listed in the Rhino 8 or Rhino 9 index; dialogs show only formats whose plug-ins are enabled.

sources.title: Is the SketchUp SDK free to use for me? (SketchUp forum)
sources.extract: C SDK access needs developer registration and agreement to Trimble API terms; SDK has its own licence; a forum answer says .skp can be read without SketchUp; cost unclear; not legal advice.

sources.title: SketchUp help: Exporting OBJ files
sources.extract: OBJ export is SketchUp Pro only; Units drop-down (default model units); polygon faces only; no hierarchy; edges optional.

sources.title: Autodesk revit-ifc (open-source Revit IFC exporter)
sources.extract: IFC add-in for Revit and Revit LT 2019+; LGPLv2; includes a proprietary Autodesk DLL usable under Autodesk terms; IFC version, MVD and georeference support not stated on the page.

sources.title: APS Free and Paid tiers announcement
sources.extract: Free tier gives monthly access with usage caps for Model Derivative; exceeding a cap suspends the API until next month; Paid: Prepay Flex tokens (minimum 100, expire after 1 year) or Pay As You Go in select countries; cap numbers are in an image.

sources.title: APS Model Derivative supported translations
sources.extract: Page is script-rendered and returned no table to my fetcher; claims about RVT, SKP and IFC input/output support are unverified; pricing of 0.5 Flex tokens per complex job came from a search snippet only.

sources.title: EPSG:26910 NAD83 / UTM zone 10N
sources.extract: Metres; 126 W to 120 W including British Columbia; central meridian 123 W; scale factor 0.9996; default NAD83-to-WGS84 transformation accuracy listed 4.0 m (remarks say 2 m).

sources.title: Universal Transverse Mercator coordinate system (Wikipedia)
sources.extract: Zone 10 central meridian 123 W; scale 0.9996 on the central meridian; false easting 500 km; grid convergence approximated as delta-longitude x sin latitude.

sources.title: Transverse Mercator projection (Wikipedia)
sources.extract: Convergence gamma = arctan(tan(lambda) sin(phi)); point scale k0 / sqrt(1 - sin^2 lambda cos^2 phi).

sources.title: proj4js
sources.extract: JS port of PROJ; predefines EPSG 4326, 4269, 3857 and WGS84 UTM zones 32601-32660 and 32701-32760 (not 26910); custom definitions via proj4.defs; accepts WKT and PROJJSON; licence not named on the page.

sources.title: CTBUH height criteria
sources.publisher: Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat
sources.extract: Height from the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance; architectural top excludes antennas and signage; floors counted above ground including significant mezzanines and major mechanical floors, excluding plant above the general roof.

sources.title: City of Vancouver open data: Building footprints 2009
sources.extract: Open Government Licence - Vancouver; 124,181 polygons derived from 2009 LiDAR; 'approximate, best used for comparison, not updated'; fields baseelev_m, topelev_m, hgt_agl, avght_m, maxht_m, bldgid; sample building 149845 has stacked parts where topelev - baseelev = hgt_agl.

sources.title: City of Vancouver open data: LiDAR 2022
sources.extract: Acquired 7 and 9 Sep 2022; about 49 points/m2; vertical accuracy 0.081 m at 95%; 181 LAS tiles from 16.45 MB to 2.74 GB; UTM 10 on NAD83(CSRS); vertical datum CGVD28GVRD; classes include buildings. The 2018 dataset (30 points/m2, 0.18 m) was also read.

sources.title: City of Vancouver open data: View cones
sources.extract: 24 polygons of protected views; building heights inside are limited; by-laws are authoritative; updated 2026-10-19; Open Government Licence - Vancouver.

sources.title: City of Vancouver open data: Property parcel polygons
sources.extract: 99,698 assessment-based polygons; 'much of the land base is created using survey accuracy however some features are not as precise'; updated 2026-10-19.

sources.title: Overture Maps buildings theme
sources.extract: ODbL because OpenStreetMap is included; sources include City of Vancouver open data; building and building_part types; height merged on IoU above 0.5; heights of 900 m or more excluded.

sources.title: COPC: Cloud Optimized Point Cloud
sources.extract: LAZ 1.4 with clustered octree; range-request streaming; only LAS point formats 6, 7 or 8; specification page shows a copyright notice and names no open licence.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.extract: Recommendation of 30 April 2013; classes Entity, Activity, Agent; properties wasGeneratedBy, used, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo.

sources.title: isomorphic-git
sources.extract: MIT; pure JS git for browser and Node; browser clone and push need a CORS proxy; LightningFS may reorder writes (call fs.flush); maintained by two volunteers.

sources.title: Measure performance with the RAIL model
sources.extract: Respond within 100 ms; process input events within 50 ms; produce frames in 10 ms (16 ms budget); idle work in chunks of 50 ms; interactive within 5 s on mid-range mobile over slow 3G, later loads under 2 s.

sources.title: Interaction to Next Paint (INP)
sources.extract: Good <= 200 ms, needs improvement 200-500 ms, poor > 500 ms at the 75th percentile.

sources.title: Claude API: Structured outputs
sources.extract: JSON-schema constrained responses and strict tool use; no numeric min/max or recursive schemas; refusals or truncation can break the schema; Sonnet 5.5 listed as supported.

sources.title: rhinomcp
sources.extract: MIT; connects Claude and other MCP clients to Rhino 8 (Windows or macOS) and Grasshopper; needs Python 3.10+, uv and a Rhino plugin.

sources.title: Online 3D Viewer
sources.extract: MIT; imports 3dm, 3ds, 3mf, dae, fbx, gltf, ifc, iges, step, stl, obj and more (skp not listed); built on three.js, rhino3dm, web-ifc and occt-import-js.

sources.title: Manifold geometry library
sources.extract: Apache-2.0; guaranteed-manifold mesh Booleans; npm manifold-3d WASM build is serial-only.

sources.title: three-mesh-bvh
sources.extract: MIT; BVH raycasting and spatial queries for three.js; 500 rays against an 80,000-polygon model at 60 fps (conditions not given); large or off-centre geometry can cause precision errors, so centre it.

sources.title: opencascade.js
sources.extract: LGPL-2.1; OpenCascade port to WebAssembly; OCCT 7.6.2 badge; no releases listed in the captured page; builds folder for custom builds.

sources.title: three.js
sources.extract: MIT; WebGL and WebGPU renderers; loader list not shown on the repo page.

sources.title: Wavefront OBJ format description
sources.extract: ASCII format; no unit stated for coordinates; no animation, lights or structured metadata; materials in a separate .mtl file; viewers differ in MTL handling.

sources.title: Vancouver Tall Challenge page
sources.extract: Brief download lists 'Site plans & 3D model' (formats not stated); registration closes 29 Oct 2026; Q&A until 3 Nov 2026; submission 30 Nov 2026 23:59 London; winners 26 Jan 2027.

sources.title: VTC brief facts as quoted in the project packet
sources.publisher: Buildner with City of Vancouver and UBC SALA
sources.extract: Site about 79.2 x 144.8 m (260 x 475 ft); towers 244-305 m; minimum 9.0 FSR non-residential high-employment area; north arrow rotated relative to the street grid. The brief PDF link on the public page is a placeholder, so the PDF was not read by me.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy for Rezonings (1997)
sources.extract: Not opened: HTTP 403. Whether it is superseded or amended could not be determined.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy Review engagement document
sources.extract: Not opened: HTTP 403.

flags.claim: City of Vancouver building footprints and heights can serve as a current context model
flags.correction: The dataset 'Building footprints 2009' is derived from 2009 LiDAR, 'approximate, best used for comparison' and 'not being updated'. Use LiDAR 2022 (about 49 points/m2) or the organiser's 3D model for current heights.
flags.detail: Data age of footprints is 17 years against 4 years for LiDAR 2022; towers built since 2009 are missing or wrong. See P14-M08.

flags.claim: Rhino can import or export IFC natively, so IFC is a universal route from .3dm
flags.detail: McNeel's Rhino 8 and Rhino 9 import/export indexes list skp, glb/gltf, obj, fbx, dwg and step, but not ifc or rvt. The page notes dialogs show only formats whose plug-ins are enabled, so a plug-in route may exist; not confirmed.

flags.claim: Rhino.Compute can be used by the student team for server-side geometry
flags.detail: Code is MIT, but it runs on Rhino 8 for Windows and core-hour billing (USD 0.10 per core-hour) is not compatible with Educational or Commercial licences. Whether the course or UBC holds a suitable licence is unknown, so it is optional and not core.

flags.claim: proj4js can transform EPSG:26910 out of the box
flags.correction: proj4js predefines WGS84 UTM zones (EPSG 32601-32660) and some others, not 26910; the module must register the NAD83 UTM zone 10N definition with proj4.defs.
flags.detail: Based on the proj4js repository page; not tested in code.

flags.claim: SketchUp .skp can be read directly with the SketchUp C SDK in an open-source tool
flags.detail: Access needs developer registration and agreement to Trimble API terms; redistribution terms were not read (forum thread only). Recommended route is export to OBJ/GLB/IFC, Speckle connector, or Rhino 8 import then save .3dm.

flags.claim: Revit .rvt can be converted to IFC or meshes through APS Model Derivative at acceptable cost
flags.detail: The supported-translations table and pricing page are script-rendered and could not be read. Free tier has monthly caps (numbers not retrieved); paid tier uses Flex tokens; per-job price came from a search snippet only.

flags.claim: IFC4X3 geometry imports reliably in web-ifc and IfcOpenShell
flags.detail: web-ifc enumerates IFC4X3 in its schema file, but the IfcOpenShell README states extensive geometry support only for IFC2x3 TC1 and IFC4 Add2 TC1. Test with a tower export before relying on IFC4X3.

flags.claim: Speckle object model is stable enough to map Layer 0 to
flags.detail: Speckle 2026.9 replaced the nested object graph with bundles (units per object, no Level object, no proxies); compatibility mode for ACC sync and file uploads ends 1 November 2026. Mapping targets may move during the project.

flags.claim: Organiser's 'Site plans & 3D model' download is in a format and CRS the tool can read
flags.detail: The public page does not state formats, CRS, vertical datum or what north arrow it shows. Q&A closes 3 November 2026; suggest asking for file formats, true versus grid north, and datum.

flags.claim: Higher Buildings Policy (1997) is the governing policy for height and view protection
flags.detail: Both policy PDFs named in the brief returned HTTP 403 to my fetcher. I could not determine whether the Higher Buildings Policy Review has superseded or amended the 1997 policy. The view-cones dataset says the City's by-laws are authoritative.

flags.claim: AI-assisted labelling accuracy thresholds (95% auto-accept precision, 80% floor)
flags.detail: The web-search budget ran out before literature on IFC/BIM element classification accuracy could be retrieved. These numbers are editable team assumptions to be measured on a labelled VTC test set.

flags.claim: IFC class definitions used in the Layer 0 mapping (IfcSpace, IfcSpatialZone, IfcMapConversion semantics)
flags.detail: buildingSMART documentation pages returned HTTP 403 to my fetcher; definitions rely on the City2BIM wiki, IfcOpenShell source, web-ifc schema listing and a search summary. Verify against the official pages before publishing.

flags.claim: All thresholds with status team_assumption in P14 (completeness, parity, overlap, true-north error, data age, 100 m tall-building cut-off, etc.)
flags.detail: Shown in the tool as editable presets with the reasoning in each metric's basis; none has a published source.

unresolved_relationships: Downtown Vancouver street-grid skew versus true north, and which north (true, grid, magnetic) the VTC site-plan arrow shows: no source opened gives the angle; derive from City parcel polygons and confirm with the organiser.
Context radius needed for shadow and wind studies as a function of tower height: no sourced relationship found; belongs to the CLIM packets.

Meaning of footprint fields avght_m, maxht_m, minht_m, base_m and the vertical datum of topelev_m in Building footprints 2009 (sample: topelev 219.29 minus baseelev 30.7 equals hgt_agl 188.59, but maxht_m is 208.63).
Which program tags count toward the minimum 9.0 FSR of non-residential, high-employment floor area (brief names office and commercial; hotel and cultural/civic open); belongs to the program packet.
Accuracy of rule-based versus LLM labelling of massing models, and the effect of the confidence threshold on override rate: no benchmark retrieved.
Floor-to-floor height priors by use for floor detection: not sourced in this packet (structure and program packets).
Whether APS Model Derivative converts RVT to IFC or meshes, and its per-job price and free-tier caps: documentation pages not readable.
Whether the SketchUp C SDK terms permit use in an open-source web tool: official Trimble API terms not opened.
Whether the Higher Buildings Policy (1997) has been superseded or amended by the Higher Buildings Policy Review: PDFs not readable.
Formats, CRS and vertical datum of the organiser's 'Site plans & 3D model' download.
How Layer 0 should map to the Speckle 2026.9 bundle format during the compatibility window ending 1 November 2026.
change_log: Round 1: first specification of packet P14 with 8 modules (M01 Layer 0 schema, M02 import pipeline, M03 units/north/georeference, M04 AI labelling and floor detection, M05 geometry health, M06 versioning and provenance, M07 browser kernel and performance, M08 City context ingest).

Priorities: core = M01, M02, M03, M05, M07; v1 = M04, M06, M08 (manual tagging and the organiser's context model are the core fallbacks). Core effort totals about 22 person-days (team estimate), tight for 13 Nov 2026.
Corrected scope assumption: City 'Building footprints 2009' is not current (2009 LiDAR, not updated); LiDAR 2022 is the current City source. Flagged FALSE_ASSUMPTION.
Corrected: Rhino.Compute is MIT code but needs Rhino 8 for Windows and core-hour billing, not compatible with Educational licences; moved out of core.
Corrected: Rhino 8 and 9 index lists SketchUp, OBJ, FBX and glTF but not IFC or Revit; IFC via Rhino is not assumed.
Corrected: proj4js predefines WGS84 UTM zones, not EPSG:26910; the georeference module registers NAD83 UTM 10N explicitly.

Derived numbers (computed here, not quoted): site area 11,468 m2 and 9.0 FSR about 103,200 m2; UTM area scale 0.08% about 83 m2; grid convergence about 0.1 deg at lon -123.12, lat 49.29; float32 step about 0.5 m at northing 5.46 million m; 1 degree error moves a 100 m shadow tip about 1.7 m.

Limitation: the shared web-search budget ran out mid-round. Not retrieved: AI-labelling accuracy literature, buildingSMART class pages (HTTP 403), City licence text, APS tables and pricing, Higher Buildings PDFs (HTTP 403), SketchUp IFC export page.
notes: Format routes (summary): .3dm = rhino3dm.js/py native (layers, object names, ModelUnitSystem, EarthAnchorPoint; B-reps need saved render meshes). OBJ = native parse, user must declare unit, no hierarchy or metadata. IFC = web-ifc in browser, IfcOpenShell server-side; ask authors for IFC2x3 or IFC4 export. glTF/GLB = native, metres, extras for metadata. FBX = loader or assimp with unit prompt (unit behaviour unverified). SketchUp .skp = no browser reader; use OBJ/GLB export (OBJ needs SketchUp Pro), Speckle connector (SketchUp 2021-2026), or Rhino 8 import then save .3dm. Revit .rvt = IFC export (open-source exporter, LGPLv2), Speckle connector (Revit 2023-2027, Windows), or APS Model Derivative (unverified). Speckle is free for students and educators per its pricing page. Before the organiser Q&A closes on 3 Nov 2026, ask for: file formats of the site/3D model, which north the arrow shows, and the datum. Source count (56) exceeds the 40 target because licence and cost facts were needed per tool; 4 sources could not be opened and are marked opened=false.
